title: 「Prologue: Declaration of Never Wanting to Work for My Entire Life
content: "Everyone! Thank you for coming to our live performance of 'Dimension Stars!' today!"
"Uwaaaaaaaahhh...!!"

In response to the echoing voice through the microphone, cheers erupted. In the dimly lit space, excitement swirled, and all eyes focused on the stage. The beautifully decorated stage featured four girls, illuminated by spotlights, smiling back at the audience.
"We'll do our best to make sure everyone is satisfied today! If you don't watch us properly... that's not okay, you know?"
The first to speak was the Black-haired Girl.
"Woooooaaaaahhhhh!!! I'll stare at youuuuuuuuuuuuuuu!!!"
"Hehe, you better not blink, okay?" The White-haired Girl smiled next.
"I absolutely won't!!! I'll cut off my eyelids!!!"
"Since we have a new song today, I hope you enjoy it... I-I mean, it's not like I would hate it if you didn't enjoy it or anything!" The Silver-haired Girl's voice rose shyly.
"Nhoooooo!!! Tsundere received!!!"
"Everyone, please enjoy yourselves! If not... it’ll be a problem, you know? ♪" The Red-haired Girl placed a finger on her lips and smiled cheekily.
"Hauuuuuuuuu!!! My heart is going to burst!!!"

With every word they spoke through the microphone, the energy in the venue intensified. Perhaps sensing this, the Black-haired Girl standing at the center nodded with satisfaction and raised her voice even louder.
"Ahaha♪ Alright! Then let's have fun! It's sudden, but here we go with the new song! 'My Boyfriend is a Loser?!'"
"Woooooaaaaahhh!!! I'm going to be a loser too!!!"
[img]https://i.imgur.com/Rf5kXqd.jpeg

The loud cheers echoed once again. Although the live performance had just begun, the audience's excitement had already reached its peak. This fervor was a clear expression of their anticipation for the show. It was something that could be felt even through the screen. However, it seemed I wasn’t the only one who noticed it. A few people walking through the streets looked up, directing their attention to the large screen overhead.

“Oh, it’s ‘Damenz’!”
“The live footage is already up, huh?”
“I can’t wait for the new song to start streaming!”
The voices expressing their thoughts reached my ears, and all of them were positive. Before I knew it, my cheeks relaxed, and a smile slipped out.
“Heh… It seems that ‘Damenz’ is steadily gaining popularity.”

The location was right in the heart of the city. Even amidst the bustling crowd, hearing such voices was proof that the popularity of ‘Dimension Stars!’ was on the rise. Among them, the names of the two girls at the center were being shouted the loudest.
“Wooooo!!! L-O-V-E! Setsuna!!! I love you!!!! Arisa!!!”

“I never thought those two would become this popular,” I muttered to myself, well aware of who they were. They were the double centers of ‘Dimension Stars!’ and the faces of the unit, effectively splitting their popularity in half. Those two, Takanashi Setsuna and Tsukishiro Arisa, were my childhood friends.
“It’s already been ten years since then. Time flies.”
And the reason those two were pursuing their idol careers was none other than me.

I don’t want to work. I think that’s a sentiment everyone has felt at least once in their lives. I, Kuzuhara Kazuma, first pondered this when I was in elementary school. The trigger was something truly trivial. At that time, there was an excursion where we ventured a bit away from school. I distinctly remember everyone around me being overly excited during the bus ride, hardly paying attention to the teacher’s talk. Even when we arrived at our destination, nothing changed.

It could be said that it was typical behavior for young children, but it must have been quite a challenge for the teacher to manage a large group of kids acting freely. I, on the other hand, wasn’t particularly excited and quietly lined up, merely observing as everyone else settled down. But then, I glanced at the teacher, who was wearing a tired expression while dealing with the kids, and I thought to myself.
—I don’t want to end up like that.

Looking back, I was quite an advanced child for my age. At seven years old, there are hardly any kids who seriously think about their future. I usually preferred to play, and I had never questioned the sight of adults working until then. It was just a given that I would work when I grew up. That was the extent of my understanding. I would only harbor dreams of the professions I saw on TV.

But at that moment, I began to wonder. What’s the point of working with such a tired expression? Once I started thinking about it, I couldn’t stop. Reflecting on it, my parents always came home late. And when they did, they wore expressions that were just as exhausted as the teacher’s. They put on smiles in front of me, but I vividly remember the moments when they sighed or looked exasperated while answering calls on their smartphones.
Would I end up making such a face in the future? The thought made me feel uneasy. Why did they have to work so hard while looking so tired?

I absolutely didn’t want to work. A strong desire not to work began to take over my entire being. The result of that was a rather unchildlike dilemma: how could I avoid working altogether? I thought about having my parents keep working while I lived off them, but that wouldn’t be enough money in the long run.

While I didn’t want to work, I wanted to live a life filled with play. I dreamed of a future where I could play and play, living an incredibly successful life. To make that dream come true, I would need a lot of money. Just living normally wouldn’t earn me that kind of money.

The quickest way to get a large sum of money was gambling, but should I really leave everything to luck? I could start saving my allowance now and try my luck with the lottery or horse racing in the future. Betting everything on a long shot for a complete reversal of fortune—that was my only option, right?
No, gambling lacks certainty. If I lost, I would have no choice but to work. I didn’t want that. I absolutely hated that! But what could I do…?
While I was pondering this over my excursion lunch, it happened.
“There you are, Kazukun.”
“Huh?”
Surprised by suddenly hearing my name, I looked up to see a girl standing there.
“Oh, Setsuna.”
“‘Oh’ isn’t enough! I was looking for you! I was really worried you got lost during the excursion!”

Peering into my face was my childhood friend, Takanashi Setsuna. Among the kids of our age, she stood out with her exceptionally beautiful features, but just like her name suggested, her skin was as white as snow, now slightly flushed. Her translucent black hair was a bit disheveled, indicating that she had truly been searching for me everywhere.
“Sorry, sorry. Want to eat a octopus sausage as an apology?”
“Is it okay!? Yay, I’ll eat it!”

Feeling a bit guilty, I held out the sausage I had speared with a fork in front of her face, and she immediately took a big bite. Perhaps because of her good athletic ability, her movements were surprisingly quick.
“Munch munch munch.”
“What’s up? Were you that hungry?”
“Swallow! …No, that’s not it. It made me really happy that Kazukun gave it to me. I really love you, Kazukun.”
“You’re being dramatic, Setsuna. I just gave you one side dish.”

I couldn’t help but chuckle. This childhood friend of mine was inexplicably attached to me. It was common for her to follow me around or come talk to me when I was alone. Recently, she had even started coming over from her house next door every morning to check if I had forgotten anything, being overly concerned for me.
That was my perception of Setsuna when we were seven years old.
“If it’s something Kazukun gives me, I’m happy with anything!”
“Is that so? Well, I’m glad.”
“Yep!”
She beamed at me with a smile as bright as the sun. Seeing such a cheerful expression made me feel a bit envious.
“…You seem to have no worries. Here I am, troubled about so much.”
Maybe that’s why? Without realizing it, my true feelings slipped out.
I immediately regretted it, but Setsuna wasn’t the type to miss such a thing. Her smile from earlier instantly transformed into a worried expression.
“What’s wrong? Were you thinking about something alone?”
“Uh, well, about earlier…”
“Are you not enjoying the excursion? Or are you feeling unwell? Should I tell the teacher and go back to the bus with you?”

She kept asking me repeatedly. It was clear she was concerned, but for me at that time, her worry was honestly more of a nuisance. While it was sometimes helpful to have her around, when I was deep in thought, it was a different story. I found it to be unnecessary meddling, even annoying at times.
“No, it’s fine. You don’t have to do that. I’ll finish eating soon, so just leave me alone.”
Maybe that’s why my tone ended up sounding rather curt.
“Oh, I’m sorry, Kazukun.”
“No, it’s not that I’m saying you’re a bother…”
“You’re probably just thinking about something useless, right? You always do that.”
Just as I was about to apologize for my tone, a voice cut in between us.
“Arisa…”
“Don’t say anything that would make Setsuna cry. Unlike Kazuma, she’s a really good girl!”

The one giving me an exasperated look was my other childhood friend, Tsukishiro Arisa. With her silver hair tied into twin tails with blue ribbons, she was just as cute as Setsuna. However, her personality was sharp, and she sometimes threw harsh words my way, making her difficult to deal with in a different sense.
“By the way, Kazuma, your mouth is dirty. Stay still, I’ll wipe it for you.”
“Oh, okay.”
“And sitting on the ground will get your clothes dirty. You’ll get scolded. I’ll lend you a handkerchief, so sit on this.”
“Y-Yeah. Thanks, Arisa.”
She had a caring side, so I couldn’t help but find her somewhat endearing. As I accepted the handkerchief, Arisa showed a smug smile.
“Hehe. I guess Kazuma needs me to take care of him.”
I didn’t particularly think anything of it, but right next to me, Setsuna took issue with it.
“Ah! Arisa-chan, that’s unfair! I wanted to take care of Kazukun!”
“Setsuna, you always stick to Kazuma before I do.”
“I like Kazukun, so it’s fine!”
“Then I like Kazuma too! I like Setsuna, but I like him too!”
“That’s not true! I like Kazukun way more!”
“I’m obviously the one who likes him more!”
“Ugh!”
“Meh!”
It seemed like Setsuna and Arisa were getting all worked up, ignoring me.
“It’s a bit troublesome to have you two fighting in front of me…”

Usually, they got along well, but for some reason, these two had a habit of competing over me. Watching them, I felt my tension dissipate, and I ended up voicing the concerns I had just been mulling over.
“Sigh… I just wanted to think carefully about a really important dilemma…”
“A dilemma?”
“Were you really troubled? If so, should I help you out? I’ll do anything for you, Kazukun!”

Suddenly, both Setsuna and Arisa stopped arguing and turned to look at me. Perhaps because they were childhood friends, their gestures were perfectly in sync, but since I hadn’t expected them to be listening, I found myself at a loss for words.
“Uh, um…”
“Speak up, Kazuma.”
“Talk to us, Kazukun.”

The two childhood friends leaned in closer. Both of them had a stubborn side, and once it got to this point, they wouldn’t leave me alone until I told them everything. But saying I absolutely didn’t want to work in the future wouldn’t lead to anything good… Wait a minute?
“Setsuna. Arisa. Can I ask you something?”
“What is it? Hurry up and say it, we’re waiting.”
“What is it!? Do you want me to do something for you!?”

Arisa looked at me with a somewhat annoyed expression, while Setsuna gazed at me with sparkling eyes. The two of them had contrasting attitudes, but I could see that Setsuna was eagerly awaiting my response.
(Perhaps… could this work?)

Looking into Setsuna’s beautiful eyes, I felt a sense of conviction. Arisa might be strict, but Setsuna was incredibly sweet to me. Back in kindergarten, she always cleaned up the toys we played with, and if I asked for dessert during lunch, she would easily give it to me.

That wasn’t all. Last Christmas, she had even bought me a toy I wanted instead of one for herself, handing it to me with a smile while saying, “You wanted this, right?” I was genuinely surprised by that, and I still didn’t quite understand why Setsuna was so devoted to me.
But there was no doubt that she wanted to take care of me. So, she would surely not refuse my proposal. With that calculation in mind, I slowly opened my mouth.
“Um, you see, I don’t want to work.”
““You don’t want to work…?””
“Yeah, I absolutely don’t want to work. I definitely want to avoid it. So… in the future, I want you two to work in my place and take care of me.”
At my proposal, both of them widened their eyes in shock.
“Huh!?”
“Me? In place of Kazukun?”
“Yeah. And I want you to support me for life.”
Was that too much? My cheerful inquiry was undoubtedly that of a loser, even for a child. Normally, it would be something that would never get a nod of agreement.
As expected, Arisa’s eyes narrowed in anger.
“Kazuma! What are you saying!? Do you realize how terrible that is!? There’s no way I’d agree to that!”
Her reaction was entirely justified, and I thought it was the right response. I would be angry too if someone said that to me, and I would definitely not agree.
“Come on, Setsuna, you have to say something too! If this goes on, Kazuma will end up being a complete loser in the future! That’s absolutely not okay!”
With her indignation still evident, Arisa turned to the black-haired childhood friend standing beside her. Perhaps she thought that Setsuna shared her anger.
However.
“……Okay, I understand.”
Setsuna was different. She briefly wore a puzzled expression, but then nodded vigorously.
“Eh… S-Setsuna…?”
“Really? You understand what I’m saying, right?”
“Yeah, of course!”
Seeing that, I couldn’t help but suppress a grin. Ignoring Arisa’s confusion, I asked Setsuna again if she would really take care of me.
“I’ll support you for life, Kazukun!”
With a beaming smile, she answered me.
“W-What about Arisa-chan? Is it okay if I’m the only one taking care of Kazukun?”
“N-No way! I’ll take care of Kazuma too! …Ugh, this is definitely wrong, but I don’t want to lose or be apart from him!”

By the way, right after this, there was a scene where Arisa, with tearful eyes, reluctantly declared she would take care of me as well. This childhood friend of mine was competitive and surprisingly lonely.
